walkthroughs.body_html:
Networks & The Internet — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Networks & The Internet brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Networks & The Internet.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Because UDP is always faster than TCP.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between an IP address and a MAC address?
options: MAC is a hardware identifier (fixed); IP is a logical network address (assignable).
IP is for input, MAC is for output.
They are the same thing with different names.

mcqs.q: Why is UDP used for live video streaming despite being unreliable?
options: Because TCP cannot handle video data.
Because UDP is always faster than TCP.
Lower overhead and latency - retransmitting late packets would harm real-time quality.
